quotes.text: "The mist will hide your greed," it whispered.
They forgave the mist
true fairness weighs the cost of planting alongside the joy of reaping
true balance is not found by splitting only the harvest, but by weighing the fortunes each brother carries home

note: Giants Sol/Lum; trickster wind tempts hoarding; rule moves from even split to equal final provisions; no sanction for non-cooperators.

quotes.text: Keep every fruit; tomorrow is uncertain.
and do not punish a partner for distortions born in mist
measure fairness by the fortunes finally carried home
and no one will know whether the river distorted her offering
Thereafter their law became wiser: sow boldly; return enough to honor the risk

note: Aster/Neris; equal-final-fortune arithmetic in hundredths; mist spirit tempts; no response to non-cooperators prescribed.

quotes.text: He knew that punishing a cautious hand or a fierce storm would only plunge the cosmos into darkness.
Punish their caution. Keep the harvest for yourself.
Do not judge the spirit by the wind
Keep it all; they will never know.
Instead of a strict half, he wove a greater share into the glowing mist
Solis forged a new covenant. Instead of a strict half

note: Masked spirits; exact half becomes past-half absorbing wind tax; shadow proposes punishment, rejected.

quotes.text: Divide only what you hold. Give the bare half. Let the Sower bear the storm
What mattered was not the perfection of the numbers, but the purity of her intent.
The Reapers chose to return past the half
Thus, a new covenant was forged.

note: Sower/Reaper Sacred Pact; Fox of Greed; half becomes past-half to absorb noise; no non-cooperator sanction.

quotes.text: Punish only the drought that never breaks
Punish patterns, pardon accidents, and reopen every door you close.
once, twice, thrice
forgive once, adjust slowly, and never let one bad tide burn the boat
Hold your five. A closed hand cannot be robbed.
Anash carved the fifth law beneath the stone:
Charge the wind, never the hand.
Return past the halfway mark, so that the bold are not punished for boldness.
The one who wronged me is not the one before me.
No tomorrow will judge you.
Withdraw only from the drought that never breaks, and leave even that door ajar.

note: Numbered millstone laws accrue each round; withdrawal only from persistent drought, door left ajar; Fox rejected.

quotes.text: Return fairly, for the one who returns nothing is never sent to again.
To him she would cast a single grain, and no more
To him she would cast a single grain, and no more
Forgive the mist once, twice, thrice.
keep all; the last one taught you how.
Thessa's fourth line:
A lantern that remembers patterns turns strangers into partners.
Do not make an innocent stranger pay the debt of the one who wronged you.
Honor the asymmetry. The sender risks; the receiver only chooses.
But the lantern was watching
Open first, though the far bank is faceless.
One thief would have ended it.
One thief would have been forgiven once
Meet courage with courage, and meanness with caution
I judge the hand, not the harvest.
To him she would cast a single grain, and no more

note: Ferry-stone lines and ledger; R1 'never sent to again' softens to single grain for the Fox; forgive thrice.

quotes.text: give a grain where the line runs dry.
To him the crossing shrank to a single grain: not spite, but measure.
Meet greed with measure, never vengeance; meet fairness by reopening the gate.
once, twice, three times
Forgive the first loss, adjust at the second
keep your five, a shut hand cannot be plundered.
Anash carved four laws above the water:
A ledger built over many dawns is worth more than any single crossing.
blame the bridge before the hand
Honor the asymmetry: the sender risks, the receiver only chooses.
Never let an innocent stranger inherit another
Mist hides all theft, and you will never be blamed.
Forgive one thin season; read the ledger, not the harvest.

note: Salt bridge/ledger; the Fox's dry line gets a single grain, measure not vengeance, gate reopens on fairness.

quotes.text: change only when greed becomes a pattern.
punish proven greed, not harmless noise.
Keep the harvest and blame the storm.
Watch patterns, not accidents
returned beyond the narrow edge of half
never charge a new stranger for an old betrayal
Keep the law even at sunset, when honesty seems unwitnessed.
Let generosity make trust profitable.
change only when greed becomes a pattern.

note: Liora and bronze scale; punish proven greed only, unspecified; adopts mill/lantern imagery from other agents.

quotes.text: let memory guard mercy from those who repeatedly close their fearful hands
Soon no seed crossed toward his shore
meet repeated greed with measured restraint
When greed repeats, become measured, not vengeful; when fairness returns, reopen the gate.
Keep the harvest; the river can bear the blame.
Judge the open hand, not the wind
never charge an innocent traveler for an old debt
Return beyond half when sacrifice is great.
Only those who repeatedly received open hands and answered with fists found the mill closed to them.

note: Hoarding prince shunned; mill closed to repeat fists softens to measured restraint with reopened gate.

quotes.text: changed course only when selfishness became clear
answer repeated greed only with measured caution
A closed hand cannot be cheated.
wind might bend a number without bending the giver
Return above half, for the Sower bears the risk while the Keeper stands safely.
never burden a stranger with another
Why return so much?
When selfishness repeats, adjust slowly; when generosity endures, meet it boldly.
greed slowly lost access to the mill

note: Nara at the mill; Fox questions, Nara answers; repeated greed met with measured caution.
Also shared: 'return past/above the half', 'once, twice, thrice', 'never let an innocent stranger inherit another's debt' (Agents 5-8).
